newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ parliament report on Peters may be delayed.
newsitem.headline: NZ parliament report on Peters may be delayed.

text.p: The New Zealand Parliament's privileges committee is now unlikely to report on a complaint against Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Tuesday, a parliamentary source said on Monday.
"There seem to be some technical glitches and the report could be delayed until Thursday because Wednesday is a day for private members bills," the source told Reuters.
The powerful committee heard evidence during parliament's recent adjournment on an allegation Peters assaulted a backbench MP in the corridors of parliament and thus committed contempt.
It had been widely expected to report back when the House resumes on Tuesday.
The source said it was unclear whether the committee needed to meet again to finalise its report, indicating there was disagreement among the members over its conclusions.
The clerk of the committee would not comment.
The report is expected to be the focus of an extensive debate with all 120 members theoretically entitled to a 10 minute speech.
The contempt allegation against Peters was made by left-wing Alliance leader Jim Anderton after a fracas between Peters and government backbencher John Banks on March 5.
Banks and Anderton said in evidence Peters had assaulted and threatened Banks outside the debating chamber after a close division over legislation to delay tax cuts.
Peters said he only put a hand on Banks to indicate he wanted to continue talking.
The privileges committee also heard a complaint, lodged by Anderton as a petition to the committee, about a separate incident on March 5.
Anderton said Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare allegedly manhandled a radio journalist who was trying to record the exchange between Banks and Peters.
Henare has apologised to the journalist for the incident.
